label: Week 34, 2026
recap:
This week, US AI policy activity was modest, concentrated mainly in California, which accounted for four items, with the United States Congress adding two more, for a total of two jurisdictions tracked. Six bill movements were recorded, meaning their status changed rather than that any became law, alongside two federal documents from the Civil Rights Commission and the Commerce Department. Ten case updates rounded out the litigation side of the ledger.

On substance, government use and transparency and disclosure each appeared twice, the latter including California SB1159, while consumer protection and discrimination showed up once via United States Congress HB10110, elections registered once, and health care appeared once through California SB1133. Three bills did not fit a specific theme. Overall, this was a quiet week, with steady but limited movement across a narrow set of themes and jurisdictions.

federal.title: Solicitation of Nominations for Membership on the NOAA Science Advisory Board (SAB)
federal.detail: The NOAA Science Advisory Board (SAB) is the only Federal Advisory Committee with responsibility to advise the Under Secretary of Commerce for Oceans and Atmosphere on long- and short-range strategies for research, education and the application of science to resource management and environmental assessment and prediction. NOAA seeks candidates with expertise in areas relevant to its mission, including Federal, State, and local government; social and behavioral sciences; artificial intelligence and machine learning; high performance computing; data management, including open access and accessibility; uncrewed systems; whale research and conservation; aircraft systems and modernization; and economic analysis, including cost-benefit evaluation of observing systems. NOAA also encourages nominations of qualified mid-career scientists and engineers.

federal.detail: Notice is hereby given, pursuant to the provisions of the rules and regulations of the U.S. Commission on Civil Rights (Commission) and the Federal Advisory Committee Act, that the Maryland Advisory Committee (Committee) to the Commission will hold a public meeting via Zoom. The purpose is for the committee to continue The purpose is for the committee to continue briefing planning on the chosen topic of artificial intelligence and its application in voting administration.
